title: Pennsylvania launches Medicare fraud hotline during open enrollment - SC Media

 Security Operations , Governance, Risk and Compliance , IAM Technologies , Threat Intelligence Pennsylvania launches Medicare fraud hotline during open enrollment
 November 13, 2026 Share By SC Staff Macro view of a whistleblower hotline in an IT company, showcasing the support for ethical reporting, suitable for corporate accountability
 The Pennsylvania Department of Aging has introduced a toll-free hotline to assist Medicare beneficiaries in reporting suspected fraud, errors, and abuse during the annual open enrollment period, as reported by Statescoop.
 The initiative, managed by the Senior Medicare Patrol program, provides confidential support to older adults navigating complex health coverage changes. Open enrollment, which continues through Dec. 7, often serves as a window for scammers to exploit confusion regarding Medicare Advantage and prescription drug plans. State officials are urging residents to remain vigilant against unsolicited calls and requests for sensitive personal information, such as Social Security or Medicare numbers.
 Beyond the hotline, the state is promoting the Pennsylvania Medicare Education and Decision Insight program, or PA MEDI, which offers independent counseling through 52 Area Agencies on Aging. This effort aligns with broader national concerns regarding improper payments in public health programs.
 Recent federal reports highlight that Medicaid Fraud Control Units recovered nearly $2 billion in fiscal 2025, underscoring the ongoing challenge of maintaining program integrity. By providing these resources, Pennsylvania aims to protect beneficiaries while ensuring they can securely compare coverage options and access necessary assistance programs.
 Source: Statescoop
